Letter of June 21, 1972, from Clearinghouse Review Officer, Indiana State Budget Agency, with attached summaries of comments from State Agencies.
Comment: This letter does not endorse the proposed legislation. The State Division of Nature Preserves asks for more definite criteria for determining when a species or subspecies is becoming endangered.

Response: This is a question relevant to the proposed legislation rather than the Environmental Statement. It is recognized, however, that criteria provided do not spell precisely which species fall under terms
criteria provided do not spell precisely which species fall under terms of the definitions. Purpose of the action is to protect and restore not only those species that now are critically threatened with extinction but also to head off the ultimate plight of species that may soon reach the same point even though they are not rare now. Criteria for endangerment must include more than population levels. A given population may be threatened depending upon (1) what the species is or which taxonomic level is involved; (2) how many separate populations are involved; (3) present population trends; and (4) the nature of the threat that is responsible for the condition that exists, among other things. In lieu of more stringent, but impractical, criteria, the proposed legislation, as well as current authority, provide guarantees that proposed listings or changes in listing will be discussed with the States or other Federal agencies involved.
Comment: Several Divisions of the Department of Natural Resources express objection to provisions of the proposed legislation which would superimpose upon the States, Federal Government authority for regulating the taking of any endangered species because traditionally the States have been responsible for regulational and all non-migratory wildlife.
